  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push three times, in this order:

         git push origin main
         git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8
         git push origin main:blinded-fable

- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and say so in your report.

152	A repair round is the rung worker again, with the checks slice, the judge's decision and the rung's section. It carries out the instructions in order, test first, and updates `REPORT.md` and `record.md`, whose texts replace the worker's; its structured result replaces the worker's too, so it describes the whole rung as it now stands. No skeptic follows it: its own test, the review and the gate check it. A repair that does not land drops the rung. No second repair round is taken.
153	
154	## Gather
155	
156	The gather composes one local commit per approved rung on `main`; nothing is merged.
157	
158	- **The order.** First, a rung goes after every rung it lands only with (`landsOnlyWith`), so that no commit on `main` holds a rung without the rungs it needs: in climb batch 17 the old rule, which compared lines across files, put rung L's `2b1cd8e63` before rung W's `743eb5286`, and that commit alone fails `LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss:37` (`reviews/batch-17-review.md`, finding 2). Then the rungs that share a file go in the ascending order of their lowest edited line in that file, so that a later hunk does not shift lines a landed record cites; a line is compared only with a line of the same file, and rungs that share no file keep the manifest's order. Where two files order one pair both ways, the pair keeps the manifest's order. Any `file:line` a record cites that an earlier hunk shifted is re-anchored by symbol. Tests cite the specification by section, never by line, so no test is re-anchored.
159	- **Each rung.** Its net diff is applied with `git apply --3way --index`. A conflict in unrelated regions is resolved by hand; one in the same logic is returned, not guessed. Its files are written from the journal where the branch lacks them, by the commands the brief renders per rung. For a repaired rung, `REPORT.md` and `record.md` are always rewritten from the repair round's texts.
160	- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there").
161	- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
162	- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
163	- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
164	- **After the rungs.** One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). One commit writes the batch's `RECORD.md`, once, last: the order and why, each rung's commit, the rows opened and closed, each skeptic's fixes and the contested rulings by commit, the rungs that did not land, the points to report, where each item for the curator went, and last, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer", each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both parts word for word.
165	
166	A rung that did not land has its `REPORT.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` taken out of its branch path by path, its findings folded under "Not landed", and its new rows added. None of its source is applied.
167	
168	Files are staged by an explicit list and `git diff --cached --stat` is read before each commit. A commit touching a path outside `explorations/` and `.claude/` carries a `historical:` line.
169	
170	## Review beside the gate
171	
172	The review and the gate start together on the gather's commits. The review reads and never builds; the gate builds and never reads the record; the gate commits nothing, so the two never commit at once. Run side by side they took 14.7 minutes per batch off the serial tail. The review stays, once (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). Its six checks:
173	
174	1. Overlaps between rungs, and what their changes do together.
175	2. Each skeptic's fix and each repair commit, as applied: it does what its finding says, its test seen failing on the worker's head and then passing in its maker's transcript, a settled fix's citation, a reverted fix gone.
176	3. The folded record: FACTS lines, `ledger.py landing-check BASE` with no finding, also none the base already had, each fixed in the review's corrections commit, no `NEW-` placeholder left where a row is cited, every closed row fixed, the handover, the revival-change material in `RECORD.md` true of the landed code.
177	4. Each specification sentence a rung listed as made false, corrected.
178	5. The points to report, with `holdsPush`.
179	6. The items for the curator, in `PLAN.md`.
180	
181	What it does with a finding:
182	
183	- A record-only or mechanical defect it fixes itself, inside `explorations/`, in one commit.
184	- A finding settled by tests and records only it routes to the next batch, as `review-routed.N` in `PLAN.md`, with no judge.
185	- A finding whose repair touches source, library, checker, interpreter or specification goes to a judge, who rules `land`, `repair`, `drop` or `stop`. `land` is for a ruling settled by tests and records after all: its steps go to the next batch and no repair runs.
186	
187	The review returns its heads before and after its corrections and every path outside `explorations/` they changed. A path the gate reads makes the gate beside it stale, and the gate runs again. Any other path is recorded beside the gate's summary.
188	
189	A review that returns nothing after three attempts holds nothing: the batch lands on its gate, and `review-missing.1` is listed.
190	
191	### A review that still blocks after its repair
192	
193	There is one judge and one repair for the review, and no second review. When the review's repair returns nothing, stops or does not land, the code findings the judge upheld are listed as `review-unrepaired.N` for the next batch. They do not hold the push (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). A step that cannot be undone that the repair reports holds it, as a rung's does.
194	
195	### A repair of tests and records only
196	
197	After a repair on the merged tree, the review's or the gate's, the whole gate runs again only when the repair, or the review's corrections, changed a path the gate reads that is not a test file: under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or `build.xml` (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs", and `fortress-repo`'s `references/gate.md`, "When to run it"). In batch 8 the gate ran a second time after a repair of one sentence of Appendix I, 24 minutes on the critical path, with tables identical but for timing (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 4).
198	
199	A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory.
200	
201	- The repair returns its heads and changed paths. In `testRuns` it lists each test file it added or changed, run in the harness on the merged tree: the files of one corpus together in one JVM (`ONE_JVM=1 junit.sh`, and one `harness-one.sh` call for the interpreter tests).
202	- The gate runs again on a code path, a changed test no passing run exercises, a run that failed, or a repair that listed nothing.
203	- After the gate's repair it also runs again unless every red line is answered by a passing run (`failingAnswered`) and no suite count fell.
204	- When a red gate stood beside the review, and the review's repair of tests only answers its lines, no gate judge or gate repair runs.
205	- When the first gate's tables stand, the commit stage appends the runs to `summary.txt` as `# repair-tests` lines, and the paths no stage reads as `# repair-ungated` lines. `gate_compare` skips `#` lines.
206	
207	`repairRerun` in the script decides.
208	
209	## Gate
210	
211	One run on the merged tree, its logs under `tmp/gate-batch-<N>/`, its three outputs written by fixed functions, never by hand. The functions of steps 5 and 7 (`gate_summary`, `gate_compare`, `last_landed_summary`, `ladder_filter`, `ladder_compare`, `mg_phases`) are in `tools/gate-functions.sh`, which the gate sources from the tree's root with `FORTRESS_HOME` set; until 2026-10-10 they were strings of the script (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, finding GA2). Its steps:
212	
213	1. The disk.
214	2. `rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS`, then `ant compileAll`, and at once the distance stage started in the background.
215	3. The library order if the build started the caches again, then two copies of the caches for the ladder.
216	4. `ant testFast`, then `ant testSystem`, never both at once, at four threads, pinned in `build.xml` (P-125, "The suites run Fortress in parallel."). Then `ant testSpecData` once an approved rung brings it into the gate, or the last landed summary has a `specdata/` row; every example must pass (P-124, "The specification's examples join the gate at zero red.").
217	5. `summary.txt` from `gate_summary`, one row per suite read from the plain-formatter files under `TEST-RESULTS/`, because the parallel tracks interleave their lines in the ant log. It ends with the `BUILD` and `Total time` lines and the machine it ran on (`# machine `, from `rung-flat-tower/machine.sh`), so that timings are read against their machine. `gate_compare` against the newest landed summary: a failure, an empty suite, a count that fell or a suite gone is red. The `system-<i>` shards are compared by their sum, since `testSystem` is one suite sharded by sorted index and a new file moves every later file along the shards; climb batch 2's gate went red on exactly that (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-2/JUDGE-gate.md`).
218	6. The four-thread atomic runs: 14 programs, three runs each, 42 lines. A FAIL, NO-PASS or compile failure is red; a timeout is re-run once.
219	7. The ladder regression (the skill's `gate.md`): the 85 files of the baseline's pass list compared on phase and output, the `Operation took` line masked, and the eighteen microGPT components compiled only. A DOWN, STDOUT or MISSING line is red unless a rung declared it.
220	8. The checker count, and 9. the distance, below.
221	
222	A red gate goes to a judge, then one repair, then one more gate. A gate red after its repair stops the batch, nothing pushed.
223	
224	### The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage
225	
226	The gate's step 8 runs the compiler's checker over the interpreter's library (`tools/checker-count/run.sh`, about 5 minutes since climb batch 13b: 387 s in 13b's gate, 303 s on batch 14's rung L's tree and under 5 minutes in its gate, against the stage's 900 s limit) and compares its total with the last landed one. That can run past the Bash tool's 300 s limit, so a rung's worker starts the stage detached with nohup and waits for it with `wait_for`, as the skill's `session.md`, "Long commands", gives them; the distance stage below runs the same way, about half an hour (26 to 29 minutes in batch 14). It answers the library route: one library, the interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks (P-37, "The library route."). The total is reported and never red (P-39). A fix can raise it, because the checker stops checking an api at its first errors, and two rungs' changes do not add. `checker_compare` is red only on a crash line no rung declared, a stale shadow (the instrumented copy no longer matching the tracked checker), or a table with no total. The overloading checker's memo is off in the stage, since it hides 27 to 35 errors depending on build order.
227	
228	A `testIsStage` rung has that stage as its test: its before is the last landed table, run once after the edit and rebuild. No program can yet be compiled against the interpreter's library, so this is the one place a permanent stage stands in for a test file.
229	
230	A rung whose every path lies under `explorations/`, `Specification/`, `Documentation/`, a test corpus, the test harness's sources, or walk's evaluator and natives runs neither stage. Both stages run only the compiler's phases (F-111, "The checker-count and distance stages read only the compiler's phases ..."; `STAGE_BLIND`).
231	
232	### The distance stage
233	
234	The full measurement of the distance to the switch-over, reported and never red (P-39). `tools/distance/run.sh` runs every stage of the checker over the fourteen components, the twelve prelude components and the two that `List` imports (F-53, F-288), in one JVM, under shadows made from the tracked sources at each run, under the compile command's own setting, read from `Shell.java` at each run, whose implicit bound is `Any` since climb batch 22c (F-289, P-42). An edit that no longer matches stops the run, and `#shadow` says STALE. It starts beside the suites right after `compileAll` and is read last; `compare.sh` prints DISTANCE DOWN, UP or SAME and what moved, and always exits 0. The commit stage lands `distance.txt` and the per-site list, `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, which the next batch's rungs read as their before.
235	
236	## No skill text
237	
238	The batch writes no skill text. Each rung's "Revival change" material goes into the batch's `RECORD.md`, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer". After the landing, the standing skill writer writes the skill from it, and a cold read of the changed parts follows ("After the landing: the coordinator's routing", step 4). One writer does the writing (the `coordinator` skill's `references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method").
239	
240	Through batch 13 the gather folded each rung's entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md`, the review could correct it there, and a cold reader read it beside the gate's tail and made a handle findable instead of deleting it. That carried question handles, decision status and batch records into a part that workers load (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there"). The batch's cold reader and its `coldread.N` and `delta-unfolded.N` items are gone with the fold.
241	
242	The commit stage checks that nothing under `.claude/` changed since the base (step 2, below).
243	
244	## Commit, and the push held
245	
246	The commit stage:
247	
248	0. Starts the quick microGPT walk check in the background, unless an earlier attempt started it (`tools/mg-run.sh`, the quick pair, about a minute; P-30, "The check of microGPT under walk after a batch must take less than a minute."). It waits for the result before it returns. Unless both programs print `ALL PASS`, `microgpt-walk.1` is listed. It holds nothing.
249	1. Copies the gate's outputs into `compile-ladder/climb-batch-<N>/gate/` and the per-site list into place. It writes the landed figures into FACTS, numbers only: "The true distance to the switch-over" and "The checker-count stage's table". It builds the specification's PDF once if a landed commit changed `Specification/`.
250	   1a. Appends the repair runs and the paths no stage reads beside the summary, where the first gate's tables stand.
251	2. Checks every commit since the base: the skill's footer, no model identifier, and a `historical:` line where a commit touches the 2012 tree. Then it runs `git diff --name-only <base> HEAD -- .claude/`, which should print nothing. Each path it prints is listed as `skill-touched.N`, for the coordinator; it holds nothing.
252	3. Pushes `main` to `origin` and to `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` and `blinded-fable`, retrying a failed push up to four times (the protocol's hard rules).
253	4. Removes each rung's worktree without `--force`, with its ignored `tmp/` and the old code's caches folder. It keeps one git refuses, and names it, since it holds uncommitted work.
254	
255	The push is held when any landed rung's worker or skeptic, the review, or a merged-tree repair reports a point with `holdsPush` true, or a malformed one: a step that cannot be undone or acts against a decision on record. The stage then pushes nothing, keeps the worktrees, and writes a "Not pushed." paragraph into `RECORD.md`; the coordinator pushes once the curator lifts it. Batch 5's push went out past an unlifted stop because nothing held it (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/RECORD.md`). A rung that did not land holds nothing.
256	
257	## Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect
258	
259	The curator's rule on gate reruns ends: "The same weighing of cost against what a rule protects applies to the other rules of the batch workflow." The rules in force from that weighing (batch N's review, `reviews/batch-N-review.md`, question 4):
260	
261	1. **The review's judge may land and route.** A ruling whose every upheld finding is settled by tests and records only is `land`: no repair runs, and its steps go to the next batch. In batch N the repair and second review for two such findings held the batch 54 minutes after a green gate and cost about 1.0M.
262	2. *(The second review beside the commit: gone with the second review, 2026-09-29.)*
263	3. **The rungs' texts come from the run's journal**, by one `journal-text.py` command per file, never pasted into a brief. In batch N pasting them cost the gather 195K tokens of brief and 88K of copying. An agent after a compaction re-reads its own brief from its transcript.
264	4. **A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking.** The text lands as the rung wrote it. The path that departs gets a ledger row and a gated `XXX` test asserting the text's rule, and the text's Appendix I entry names that row among its departures. The mismatch goes to the curator as `gather.N`. A mismatch the decisions settle is fixed on the side they settle.
265	5. **A rung does not run a stage its edit cannot move** (`STAGE_BLIND`, above). In batch N rung K, an interpreter-only edit, ran the checker count twice and read the landed total twice.
266	6. **A repair's new tests run together in one JVM**, one corpus at a time (`ONE_JVM=1 junit.sh`), since a test that passes alone can fail beside others. The next batch's gate runs them in the whole corpus.
267	
268	## After the landing: the coordinator's routing
269	
270	The coordinator's steps after a landing, in this order, each done whole:
271	
272	1. The landing report to the curator.
273	2. The routing: every open row, record default and item for the curator filed with a batch or as a parked line of `PLAN.md`. Each is checked against POSITIONS and the notes `INDEX.md` lists before it is called open, put to the curator or briefed. In the same pass the routing moves out of `PLAN.md` each item the batch built or answered, and any item it finds stale: word for word, into `PLAN-history.md`, under the landing's dated heading and the heading the item stood under. The batch's own line in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its review. An open item whose text also stands in another home (a `review-queue.md` entry, a ledger row, a FACTS or POSITIONS entry) becomes one line in `PLAN.md`: what is asked, its default, and a pointer to that home. No other step takes an item out of `PLAN.md`, which held 519K characters before its consolidation of 2026-10-15, 54 % of them closed (`process-engineering/plan-map.md`, sections 2 and 4).
274	3. FACTS consolidated as its README says, superseded text moved to `FACTS-history.md`. The commit stage has already written the landed count and distance.
275	4. The skills, in three moves:
276	   - One task for the standing skill writer (`tools/skill-writer.sh`, its brief `skill-writer-brief.md`): the batch's revival-change material, the section "Revival changes, for the skill writer" of its `RECORD.md`; the skill sentences that the post-batch review lists as false; and any `skill-touched` item. The writer runs `tools/skills-lint.py` before each commit.
277	   - A cold read of the parts the writer changed, by an agent given only the skill and `skill-cold-read-brief.md`.
278	   - The writer fixes the cold read's flags, and the coordinator pushes its commits.
279	5. The next batch launched only after that, so that its workers read the updated skill (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
280	6. The combined post-batch review, started at the landing, since step 4 takes its list of false skill sentences (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
281	
282	The review explains every new or risen row of the checker count by a named rung edit. It reads the microGPT walk check's result. It reports the batch's measures against the batches before it with `tools/batch-measures.py` on the run's directory (`batch-redesign.md`, "The measures").
283	
284	## An agent that comes back with nothing
285	
286	Every `agent()` call goes through `callAgent`. A null result, an undefined one and a thrown error are treated alike, and the role runs up to two more times. A retry's prompt opens with a head saying an earlier attempt ended without its result, and listing what it may have left and how to continue from it:
287	
288	- the branch's log and status, `tmp/`, a background step still running;
289	- for the gather, the merged-tree repairs, the gate and the commit: do not apply a patch or run a finished step twice;
290	- for a skeptic: its fix commits since the worker's head, and `SKEPTIC.md` if written.
291	
292	Each retry's label carries its attempt number, so it gets its own journal key. In batch 6 the API's safety filter blocked a second skeptic's next message after it had returned its verdict, and the old script dropped the rung (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "The Workflow tool").
293	
294	### A usage limit stops the run and decides nothing
295	
296	The run stops, and decides nothing, in two cases:
297	
298	- `agent()` throws an error that names a usage or rate limit (`LIMIT_ERROR`); the role is not run again.
299	- A rung worker, a skeptic or a judge returns nothing after its three attempts.
300	
301	Once stopped, `callAgent` throws at the head of every attempt without starting an agent. No rung is marked dropped, withheld or not landed, and the gather does not start. The error says how to resume: `resumeFromRunId` with the same script and args, once the cause is gone. The finished agents come back from the journal.
302	
303	In batch 7b the weekly limit returned null for every agent, and the old script read each null skeptic as a refusal and each null judge as a drop (`reviews/batch-7b-review.md`, finding 1).
304	
305	The gather, the review, the gate, the commit and a merged-tree repair that return nothing, with no limit thrown, keep their own paths:
306	
307	- the gather unresolved;
308	- `review-missing.1`;
309	- the gate run once more;
310	- `review-unrepaired.1`.
311	
312	## How the script is checked
313	
314	Nothing is launched to check it.
315	
316	- `node explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js [SCRIPT] [--sizes RUN_DIR] [--dump DIR] [--skill SKILL_DIR]` runs the script as the Workflow harness runs it, its text with `export const meta` made `const meta` as an async function body (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "The Workflow tool"), with its globals stubbed. It runs once per scenario and compares the agents called, in order, and the result with what the scenario expects. It also checks every brief: no `undefined`, the head and the skill named, no `run_bg`, no person named outside `PLAN.md`'s heading, each role's own commands. And it checks that every section the script cites by name is a heading of its file.
317	- `--sizes` compares the briefs with a real run's first messages.
318	- `--dump` writes every brief for reading.
319	- `--skill` checks the citations against another skill tree, such as one not landed yet.
320	- The batch's `check<N>.js` checks the manifest block in a scratch copy and splices it.

# Keeping the record

How workers read the record, and edit it when a brief asks, is `fortress-repo`'s records part.

**history**
: `FACTS-history.md` or `POSITIONS-history.md`. Under each number, one block per change: a provenance line (the time, the kind of change, the report section, the commit, who, why) and the line as it stood before.

**pointer**
: Another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, with a few words on its subject: "It builds P-48, on a type parameter that a call does not fix."

**pass**
: Your rewrite of what a worker wrote into entries of the form below.

## What an entry is

An entry reads on its own. A reader who knows the language, or can look it up in the `fortress-repo` skill, can tell what it says without the conversation or the batch behind it. The entry lets a worker or you act right without opening the report, and says when the report is needed. Its number is permanent and never reused. Its title and text are rewritten freely, since the number is the key.

- A FACTS entry holds, after its number and a bold title that states the fact: what is established now, and under which conditions; what it means for the work, such as what it blocks or which row or decision it bears on; its evidence: the test that gates it, or its source, and whether it was observed, read in the code or inferred; the decision it builds, by number and subject; and the report section that holds the detail.
- A POSITIONS entry holds, after its number and a bold title: what the curator decided about the project, and why, in one or two sentences; where it applies; and what it requires of the work. It may point to a fact that it rests on, in the sentence that needs it. `P-48+` finds every fact that points to it.
- POSITIONS holds only the curator's decisions. A choice that a worker made and landed without the curator's word is a fact about the tree. Its FACTS entry says that a worker chose it, and its review-queue item names that entry.
- An entry states the present, or what holds for all time. It holds no plan and no status: no state words such as "Built." or "Still to build:", no PLAN phase or item, no review-queue item, and no words that it waits for the curator's review. PLAN and the review queue name the entries that their items concern.
- If the tree does not yet do what a decision or the team's design asks, the missing part is a row of the gap ledger. The entry may name it as "row N", with a few words on what the row holds. In an entry, "row N" always names a row of the gap ledger.
- A pointer that stays in an entry carries a few words on what it holds, such as a ledger row's subject. A bare list of numbers goes to the history.
- A handle that only made sense in a past conversation, such as "answer 9", goes to the history.
- Quote the curator only where the exact words are the decision. Otherwise condense the words into the position, keeping the part of the rule that cuts. Check the condensed text against the words before you write it. The dictated words go to the history, with their time.
- A count that each landing changes has one entry with its current value, what it counts, the kinds with the largest share, and how to read a move. Other entries give its number. A count from one measurement says so.
- An entry holds one claim that can be kept up to date on its own, with its conditions, exceptions and evidence. Split an entry when its claims answer different questions and change apart. Before you split, look for an entry that already holds the claim, and move the text there. After a split, grep the record for the old number, and repoint each pointer that meant the claim that moved.
- If several entries together establish a conclusion that workers keep working out again, make it a sentence of the entry that owns its subject, with pointers to the entries it rests on. The pass updates it when one of them changes. Add a new entry only if no entry owns it. Leave a conclusion nobody has checked in its report, out of the entries.
- Keep an entry near 600 characters. This is a check, not a cap, and no reason to split: an entry may pass it if a question below keeps a sentence.
- Write halfway to ASD-STE100.

Ask of each sentence, and act on the answer:

1. Would the reader do otherwise without it? Keep it.
2. Would the reader misread another sentence without it? Keep it.
3. Does it tell how the fact came about: a date, a batch, a correction? Move it to the history.
4. Is it detail needed only while doing the work: a line number, a list of sites, a timing? Leave it in the report, and name the section.
5. Does another entry or a skill say it? Give that entry's number, or the skill's part.
6. Can a reader new to the project follow every word? Name the kind of each count.

In a consolidation of FACTS, judge each entry by six checks. Mark each one pass, fail, or unresolved where evidence is still needed, and quote the passage that fails:

- Scope: the title and the text agree on the path, the conditions and the limits, and claim no more than the evidence shows.
- Present meaning: a reader can tell the current property, or a measurement bounded to its day, without rebuilding a batch's work.
- Evidence: the cited support exists and holds the claim, and the entry states the kind of its evidence and its uncertainty.
- Comprehension: a reader can restate the fact and what it means. Subjects, referents and terms are plain.
- Ownership: the entry has one subject. No repair history or copied count hides it.
- Consistency: entries on the same subject agree, or state their different scopes or their conflict.

An entry that fails scope, evidence or consistency is not kept as it stands: reword it to what its support holds, or investigate where the support is unresolved. A fail of comprehension or ownership asks for a rewrite. Give no score: good prose does not make up for an unsupported claim. Then give the entry one disposition:

- keep: every check passes;
- reword: the meaning holds, but the wording or the stated scope fails;
- reorganize: move detail out, merge the entry into its owner, or split it;
- investigate: the support or the consistency is unresolved. Settle that narrow question before any new wording, and do not delete the fact meanwhile.

Before you write or check the first entries of a consolidation, read the five worked examples: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-rule-draft.md#Worked examples'`, a large read.

## Reading and writing

- `git log -S'F-87' --oneline -- explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` lists the commits that touched an entry.
- To read a history in depth, or a report's passage, send a Sonnet scout. The provenance lines tell it where to dig.
- `record.py`'s header gives its usage. `add`, `set`, `merge`, `remove` and `apply` write; each needs `--from PATH#HEADING` or `--note WHY`. The tool stamps the time and copies the earlier line to the history.
- Before every commit, run `record.py check --base <the commit before your edits>`. It shows that nothing was lost, and reports each entry over 600 characters.
- Commit the record file and its history together.
- Write a decision into POSITIONS in the next commit after the curator states it. A proposal of yours enters only at the curator's yes.
- The record is public and names models on purpose. Hold nothing back from it for that.

## The pass

Run the pass when a worker finishes, and before the next boot or batch reads FACTS. In a batch, the commit stage runs it, with this part quoted in its prompt. After a lone worker, you run it.

The pass owns each entry's final wording. A rung writes its findings as draft entries: the claim, its conditions, its evidence and what it means.

1. Write each new fact as an entry, or rewrite in place the entry that it changes. A rung writes its entries in a file `record.md` in its worktree, and the gather folds them in with `record.py apply`.
2. Give each change its provenance: the report section, the commit, and why.
3. Check each entry against its source, with bounded `grep`s:
   - The cited report section holds what the entry left out.
   - The entry keeps the source's scope: the path (walk or the compiled path), the call form (a dotted method call against a top-level call), the range of values and the conditions. Ask: does the entry let a reader conclude more than the evidence shows?
   - If a behaviour changed, grep FACTS for it, linked or not. Each entry that states it is updated, or says how it differs.
4. Cut any plan or status from each entry (above). If the cut text named a PLAN item or a review-queue item, check that the item names the entry.
5. Report each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its extra sentence.

Run the same pass on POSITIONS at each landing, and when the curator replaces a decision.

## A consolidation

A consolidation runs the pass over whole sections. Run it on FACTS before each batch launches, since the batch's workers read it.

- Split each section into chunks of 20 to 32 entries.
- For each chunk, a Sonnet scout gathers each entry's report sections, its commits and the curator's dated words.
- An Opus writer reads this part, the chunk and the scout's file, and writes an apply file. It runs `apply` and `check --base` in its own worktree.
- You apply each file on `main`, run `check --base`, commit and push.
- Have Opus workers check each new entry by the pass's step 3. Run no Fable review of the entries.
- Have a fresh Opus worker answer a small quiz of decisions from the new entries, on the records at hand, without the curator. The decisions must stay as good, and the worker must follow the pointers when needed. If something critical is lost, find the middle ground entry by entry.

## The consolidation tools

Three Workflow scripts make the record and the worker skill readable again when they drift. Each one's README says how to run it and what to do with its output. Put the open questions of their runs on the review queue.

- The mining workflow finds where each POSITIONS entry came from: the curator's words, or an agent's summary or default. Run it on the entries that it has not traced, before the clarity workflow rewrites them. Its README: `explorations/coordinator/positions-audit/README.md`.
- The clarity workflow rewrites POSITIONS or FACTS entries so that each reads on its own. For FACTS, it first judges every entry by the six checks of "What an entry is" (scope, present meaning, evidence, comprehension, ownership and consistency), and rewrites only those marked reword or reorganize. Run it when entries no longer read on their own. Its README: `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/README.md`.
- The orientation workflow writes `fortress-repo`'s revival part, the short account of how revived Fortress differs from the original, which every worker reads whole. Its consolidate mode rewrites the whole part. Run it when a cold read or the regression quiz shows that the part no longer reads whole, or when an update cannot keep it within the README's budget. Its update mode runs after each landing (`references/batch.md`, "The landing"). Its README: `explorations/coordinator/tools/orientation/README.md`.

## INDEX and the gap ledger

- Give each new note under `explorations/` one line in INDEX, from its header comment's first sentence.
- Put a run's working files in an `evidence/` folder beside its results file: its briefs, chunks and checks, and the worker reports that the results draw on. Move them there with `git mv` once the results are judged. Only the results file gets an INDEX line. `check-index.sh` skips evidence folders. Do not add a folder's name to its list to let the folder pass.
- The gap ledger keeps its rows in topic sections. A row keeps its number for good. `explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py` is the only way to write it. Other views, such as `explorations/apl/lessons.md`, are derived from it.
- Split a rewrite of the ledger among small workers, each with a slice of rows that it can hold. Run a duplicate search first, as its own step.
- Ask the curator before you regroup the ledger's rows or derive its views again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  note N [--correcting TIME]     a noted block in N's history, N unchanged; needs
                                 --note; refused when the history holds it already.
                                 TIME: 2026-10-13 19:07Z, or 2nd 2026-10-14 04:41Z
      record.py note P-25 --from 'positions-audit/full/evidence/corrections-c1.md#History lines the tool cannot write' --note 'his message behind the text: 2026-09-26T08:01:03.475Z, ...'
      record.py note P-7 --correcting '2026-10-13 19:07Z' --commit b87a17de5 --note 'that block names bc8902f47, ...'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
